tasks.short: Program numerically controlled tools and electronic instruments

steps.what: Check machining requirements and define the intended program operations
Program computers or electronic instruments using suitable machining cycles
Verify the program through simulation, checks and controlled prove-out

tasks.design: Configure reusable approved cycles in the existing machining programming software {OTHER}. The machinist selects and checks parameters, inspects the generated program and retains simulation and controlled prove-out before any production use; this design does not add model control of machinery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated low-level cycle entry can duplicate known machining structures.
tasks.enabler_now: Native parameterised cycles can reduce repeated entry when appropriate to the work.
tasks.still_hard: Tool access, fixturing, material behaviour and proving a program safe on the actual machine.
tasks.human_edge: The machinist recognises when a reusable cycle is inappropriate and can stop or redesign the operation.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated cycle entry with programming judgement and prove-out intact.

reach.task: Review a reusable cycle and its limits with the machinist

evidence.claim: Native machining cycles and parameterised libraries can reduce repeated program entry, while machine-specific verification remains; this is model knowledge, not a measured case from the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is machinist programming and controlled prove-out, excluding routine production machine time. Existing automatic tool motion earns no labour saving.

Machinist produces drawing revision, material, machine/controller, coordinate system, tooling, fixture limits and intended operations in s1 with all 30 hours retained. s2 retains 30 hours including parameter capture, cycle selection, generated-code inspection and manual exceptions.
No structured model or ready machining strategy is assumed. Missing parameters or unsuitable geometry require manual programming; native cycles are tested before custom code.

s3 contains positive time for version checking, simulation and controlled prove-out under existing safe-work arrangements. Approval binds program, postprocessor, setup, tooling and fixture versions; any change requires renewed checking. It does not authorise unattended production.
unknowns: Repeated-entry burden and local prove-out authority
research_questions: Can reusable cycles reduce total programming time while retaining all prove-out and collision checks?

already_counted.description: Cycle selection, parameter capture and generated-code checks

incremental.description: Maintain cycle versions and revalidate affected setups

approvals.approved_version: Exact program checksum, postprocessor, machine, setup, tooling and fixture snapshot; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=30+30+30=90; gross 10 minus 3 upkeep gives net 7. High requires repeated suitable cycle entry; low removes only 3 hours, consumed by upkeep. Requirements and prove-out time retain their full shares.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study engineering information to determine machining methods and sequences

steps.what: Study sample parts, blueprints, drawings and engineering information
Determine methods and sequences of operations needed to fabricate products

tasks.design: Keep interpretation and machining-method selection with the machinist, using current drawings in {DOCS} and the existing engineering viewer {OTHER}. This boundary does not assume a clean geometric model or a preselected operation sequence that software can simply consume.
tasks.previous_blocker: Methods depend on tolerances, datum choices, material, access and real shop constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital production-record and gear-calculation capabilities do not establish an automatic method planner for arbitrary parts.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a feasible sequence when several constraints conflict or drawings are incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: The machinist can identify an unmanufacturable requirement and seek clarification before creating scrap.
tasks.altitude: No change to method-planning time or engineering approval rights.

reach.task: Discuss a proposed machining sequence and unresolved drawing questions

evidence.claim: Arbitrary part interpretation and method selection require engineering judgement; unrelated logging or gear-dimension tools do not establish a general planning saving.

assumptions: Boundary is interpreting supplied engineering information and selecting methods, excluding program entry and later production.

Engineering supplies the drawing and revision through existing work. Machinist produces interpreted requirements in s1 and the proposed sequence in s2; no structured feature or operation list is assumed free.
Viewer software is {OTHER}; native search and viewing are baseline. Review native capabilities before any future custom proposal.
No new software or maintained process is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Part complexity and engineering data format
research_questions: Which recurring part family has sufficiently explicit geometry and constraints to test a bounded planning aid?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Standard and complex part planning retain interpretation and method-selection time; no structured planning input is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor feed and speed during machining

steps.what: Monitor the feed and speed of machines during machining

tasks.design: Keep process observation with the machinist using machine-control indications {OTHER} and direct cutting observations. Production-state collection can support records, but does not establish that the operator can safely leave this monitoring duty.
tasks.previous_blocker: Chatter, wear, chip evacuation and changing cut conditions need situational interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Available production logging does not by itself replace feed and speed supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing subtle process changes before they damage a tool, part or machine.
tasks.human_edge: The machinist combines sound, appearance and experience to recognise an unsafe or deteriorating cut.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring time and intervention responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Report a change in cutting behaviour with current indications

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X collects produced quantities and machine statuses; the digest does not establish safe replacement of human cutting-condition monitoring.

assumptions: Boundary is human monitoring, excluding production reporting and program development.
Controller produces current feed and speed indications through existing operation; machinist observes cutting condition in retained s1. No structured safe-cutting label is assumed.
Existing controller runtime is baseline and earns no labour saving. Native condition information should be reviewed before any future custom monitoring proposal.
No change to safety control, staffing or unattended operation is introduced; upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Machining process risks and local monitoring requirements
research_questions: What validated process-specific evidence would be needed before any supervision time could safely change?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Stable and changing cuts retain human monitoring; automated count collection is not credited as removed supervision.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with programmers to verify programs and output specifications

steps.what: Confer with numerical control programmers about programs, machinery and output specifications

tasks.design: Retain the technical discussion using the exact program and test findings in machining software {OTHER}. The machinist and programmer reconcile function and specification concerns; this task does not introduce automatic correction or machine release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Program intent and real machine behaviour can disagree in ways that need technical discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared digital views aid discussion but do not establish a reduction in the actual verification conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving why a program behaves differently from the intended setup or output.
tasks.human_edge: The machinist can explain physical evidence the programmer cannot infer from code alone.
tasks.altitude: No change to consultation time or machine-release authority.

reach.task: Trace a reported output issue to the exact program and setup version
reach.learn: Physical process context and version-bound communication

evidence.claim: Technical verification discussion remains human work when intent, setup and observations must be reconciled; no separate removable preparation step is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is machinist participation in the verification discussion, excluding programmer labour, test execution and program editing.

Programmer produces the program version and setup details; test personnel or the machinist produce test findings in existing work. Their capture is unchanged and no free structured defect code is assumed.
Current machining software is {OTHER}; native shared views are baseline and earn no new saving. Review native facilities before future custom work.
No approval to run machinery is implied by the discussion. No new process is introduced, so upkeep is zero. Overlap with programming prove-out must be allocated once.
unknowns: Current discussion triggers and programme ownership
research_questions: Are delays caused by missing versions or by the technical discussion itself?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Routine and disputed verification conversations retain their time; programme preparation is counted only in its own task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated cycle entry where native reuse is suitable while retaining method judgement, prove-out, process monitoring and technical consultation.
reach: Work with numerical control programmers on explicit setup versions and unresolved machining evidence
role.ambitious_version: A machinist who uses reliable reusable programming structures and remains accountable for what the physical process actually does.
